=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:331-355 | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The skipped files summary is only rendered when `HAS_UPDATES` is true, so runs that only skip files hide the skipped list.
  WHY: `HAS_UPDATES` is based on created/updated files, so skipped-only runs omit the summary block; reviewers agreed this is an observability gap and gave the highest stated severity as medium.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:153-172 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `validation_ok=true` success signal is ordered too early relative to the rest of the step’s output/validation state.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on impact and one noted it may already be acceptable, so the highest concrete concern is a low-severity ordering/contract issue rather than a runtime bug.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:15-61 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The guardrail test checks only a specific `cp` ordering and does not comprehensively enforce all mutation points or the skipped-files placement contract.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers noted the assertion is narrow and could miss future mutation paths or the exact skipped-files visibility bug; severity is low because it is test coverage, not current runtime failure.
- .codex-workflow-src:submodule | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The PR modifies the `.codex-workflow-src*` support checkout submodule, which is forbidden by the stated guardrail.
  WHY: This was the only reviewer to flag the submodule change, but it was described as a hard block and thus retains critical severity.
- .codex-workflow-src-main:submodule deletion | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The PR deletes the `.codex-workflow-src-main` submodule, which is also forbidden by the stated guardrail.
  WHY: This is the same class of hard-block submodule modification, separately reported by one reviewer.
- working tree untracked files (.codex-workflow-src-main/ directory, scripts/review_commit_changes.sh, scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh) | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: Untracked workspace artifacts appear to be leftover AI operations and are not part of the PR manifest.
  WHY: This is a single-reviewer workspace hygiene finding with medium severity because it could pollute the PR if committed.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:331-355 | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Skipped files list is only shown when `HAS_UPDATES = true`, but `HAS_UPDATES` is only `true` when `TOTAL_CHANGED > 0`.
  WHY: Operators won't see which files were skipped in the workflow summary, reducing visibility into the update process.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:162-164 | severity=3 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `printf` operations to write output files (`/tmp/updated_files.txt`, `/tmp/created_files.txt`, `/tmp/skipped_files.txt`) have no error checking.
  WHY: Summary step would read empty or missing files, potentially showing incorrect or missing information.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:33 | severity=3 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Test only checks that the first `cp` operation appears before success signal, not that all file mutation operations happen before success signal.
  WHY: If a future change adds another mutation point with a different pattern, the test might not catch it.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:153-155 | severity=2 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Success signal (`validation_ok=true`) is emitted before `has_updates` is computed and set.
  WHY: Could cause issues if downstream consumers check `validation_ok` before other outputs are logically consistent, though GitHub Actions output semantics likely prevent actual race conditions.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:331-351 | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The code only renders the "Skipped files" summary block if `HAS_UPDATES` is true.
  WHY: Users won't see diagnostic feedback about which files were skipped unless there is also at least one actual update or creation in the same run.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:156-158 | severity=3 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Moving the `validation_ok=true` success signal after the loop that performs `cp` (mutations) weakens the guardrail contract.
  WHY: The intention of the guardrail test is to ensure no mutations happen after a success signal is emitted, and the current placement still allows accidental additions between the loop and the signal.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:32 | severity=4 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test only validates that one specific `cp` call occurs before the success signal.
  WHY: It fails to provide a comprehensive guardrail and could miss later mutation operations added in a different line/style.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:168-172 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `has_updates` flag is set based only on `TOTAL_UPDATED + TOTAL_CREATED`, so skipped-only runs do not show the skipped files summary.
  WHY: Users lose visibility into what activity occurred when all files are skipped, even though the workflow still completes successfully.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:132-137 | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The success signal ordering issue is not present in the current code.
  WHY: The reviewer explicitly concluded the code correctly places `validation_ok=true` after the `cp` operations, so this is not a valid finding.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:32 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The test asserts only one specific `cp` pattern comes before `validation_ok=true`.
  WHY: A future mutation added with a different operation could escape this narrow guardrail, though the current critical path is covered.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:331 | severity=3 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The skipped-files summary is nested inside the `HAS_UPDATES` check.
  WHY: If the only activity is skipping files, the run produces no summary output showing what was skipped.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:331-348 | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Skipped files summary is only rendered when HAS_UPDATES=true, but skipped files can occur even when no updates/creations happen.
  WHY: When only files are skipped, the summary omits the skipped list and reduces observability and auditing.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:153-159 | severity=4 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The success signal `validation_ok=true` is emitted before the data outputs `templates_checked`, `templates_updated`, `templates_created`.
  WHY: The reviewer judged this weakens the logical ordering contract even though the current runtime risk is low.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:61 | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test asserts the presence of skipped-files strings but does not assert that they are placed outside the `has_updates` conditional.
  WHY: The bug persists because CI does not guard the actual skipped-files visibility contract.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:15 | severity=3 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test only checks one specific `cp` line’s ordering relative to upstream-dir validation.
  WHY: It does not verify all mutation points or future added mutation operations.
- .codex-workflow-src (submodule) | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR modifies a runtime support checkout submodule pointer.
  WHY: This was described as explicitly forbidden by the system guardrail and must trigger human review.
- .codex-workflow-src-main (submodule deletion) | severity=5 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR deletes the `.codex-workflow-src-main` gitlink submodule.
  WHY: This is the same forbidden `.codex-workflow-src*` modification class and must not be changed.
- working tree untracked files (.codex-workflow-src-main/ directory, scripts/review_commit_changes.sh, scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh) | severity=4 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: These untracked files appear to be artifacts of local AI operations and are not part of the PR.
  WHY: They could confuse subsequent steps or enter the PR if accidentally committed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
